summary: Ob Nixilis broods over his two defeats, the first taking his body and the second his spark, and the folly of seeking the Veil.
quote: The first robbed me of my body. The second of my spark.

summary: Deep underground, Ob Nixilis rotates the hedrons on the cavern walls and casts spells, testing their runes.
quote: He rotated a hedron a few degrees and spoke a brief incantation.

summary: Ob Nixilis recalls hating Zendikar and its people, and sees Nahiri's face in each of the kor.
quote: Because in each of their smug, chalky faces, I see her .

summary: Flashback: Ob Nixilis was drawn to Zendikar to purge a curse but was attacked and bound with a hedron by Nahiri, which stopped his curse but crippled him.
quote: I couldn't even scream as she bound the hedron into me.

summary: Flashback: As the passage crushes in around him, Ob Nixilis drains the stone's vitality and digs toward a green glow.
quote: He bought himself a moment by bracing himself between the walls, and he muttered a spell.

summary: Ob Nixilis reveals that the bound hedron took his power and that his wings fell off, leaving him small and weak, and vows revenge.
quote: The thing she put inside me made me small. Weak.

summary: Ob Nixilis studies the hedrons for centuries and lures planeswalkers, letting word of his condition spread until a proud planeswalker comes to extract the hedron.
quote: And sure enough, some arrogant child finally took my lure.

summary: Ob Nixilis reaches the glowing source in the depths and takes a flower of green and gold power from a tiny sphere of life, laughing.
quote: It radiated power, warmth, and health.

summary: Ob Nixilis says that heroes coming to fight the Eldrazi will need what he knows about the hedrons, and that he feels his spark within reach after Bala Ged's destruction.
quote: My spark is within reach.

summary: Flashback: wounded at the battle of Child's Wall, Dovid lies feverish in the cathedral courtyard after Avacyn appears.
quote: and then a blinding light when, at last, Avacyn appeared.

summary: Avacyn, with the angel Gryta, summons Dovid and orders him to prepare the forbidden space of the Lofts of Thraben Cathedral.
quote: You, and you alone, must prepare that space previously forbidden.

summary: Dovid becomes Comitant Dovid, isolated from the cathars and church officials, carrying the first sword forged from the Helvault.
quote: That is how I became Comitant Dovid.

summary: Gryta opens a bricked window into the Lofts for Dovid and tells him to clear the cistern.
quote: The bricked window folded into itself silently

summary: Dovid is given Eost, a sword forged from the Helvault, with his name at the top of the honored list.
quote: I have drawn it only once, during the ceremony where it was presented to me, when Avacyn touched its point.

summary: In the cistern Dovid finds a preserved, strangled man in black with a book in his coat, which he seals in a nameless crypt and takes the book.
quote: He had been strangled, and although there were no signs of rot, he was murdered some time before

summary: Dovid solves the Nightfall Cathars' spell on the journal and learns that Avacyn had been sealed with Griselbrand and that church power diminished, a secret kept from the congregation.
quote: Avacyn had been sealed in the Helvault with the demon Griselbrand, and during that time our power had diminished.

summary: The journal reveals vampires were created by humans: Markov and the demon Shilgengar used an angel's blood, after trapping and draining Marycz.
quote: Markov and his sons trapped the angel Marycz in his laboratory and exsanguinated her

summary: The journal says Sorin created Avacyn to hold the vampires in check and that the church keeps humans as livestock, never able to defeat them; Dovid concludes his faith is a lie.
quote: We are livestock. We are unwitting participants in our own cultivation.

summary: Young Surrak enters a dark cave and has a vision of beasts on the ceiling and a human fighting a bear and winning with a double-bladed staff.
quote: Look now, young one , it seemed to say, although it held no words.

summary: Surrak follows the inward chant to the wilds and tracks a giant bear in the snow.
quote: Each print was as big around as the youth's waist, driven deep into the snow.

summary: Surrak fights the huge bear bare-handed with his claw gloves, is smashed and scarred and loses an eye, but wins by punching it and tearing at its neck until it retreats.
quote: Finally it dropped its gaze and turned aside.

summary: Surrak returns to Karakyk with trophies and is given the rights of the grown and a greatspear by the elders.
quote: They acknowledged the gifts and bestowed on Surrak the rights and titles of the grown.

summary: Surrak leads a growing band of clan fighters, soon second only to the Dragonclaw and Hunt Caller in blades.
quote: From that day, he led clan fighters to hunt both game and foes.

summary: Weary from pursuing Sultai raiders, Surrak's party catches a group of scavengers and shambling dead under three serpent-folk, including their own lost clansfolk.
quote: The Temur spat curses as they recognized the emaciated forms of their own clansfolk, lost to hunger and disease.

summary: Outnumbered Temur are overrun until the cave bear bursts in and rips through the Sultai ranks to Surrak's side, turning the battle.
quote: The cave bear crashed into the ranks of the Sultai, ripping apart the gaunt zombies

summary: After the Temur victory, Surrak sends the dying poisoned bear to the ancestors with the ancient chant and kills it with his spear.
quote: Then he stood and drove his spear through the beast's skull.

summary: He Who Whispers Twice marks Surrak as the First Father of the Temur, giving him a bearskin cloak and gauntlets made from the bear's paws.
quote: He Who Whispers Twice spoke the invocation that marked Surrak as the First Father of the Temur.

summary: Sorin arrives on Tarkir in search of the spirit dragon Ugin, led by an oracle's visions toward a dragon-head mountain peak.
quote: Somewhere up there was his destination.

summary: Sorin dominates a warrior sentry and drains him dry to feed.
quote: drained him to a pale husk.

summary: Sorin worries over Nahiri's silence and Ugin's absence while the Eldrazi titans rampage on Zendikar.
quote: The Eldrazi titans were a fire that could not be quenched, and Ugin's absence was strange.

summary: A Temur band mistakes Sorin for a Sultai demon-spawn and Sorin kills two warriors with death magic and raises them as vampire thralls.
quote: Sorin reached out his hand and willed the two leathery corpses back from the dead.

summary: Sorin turns Rushka against his captain, who beheads him, and a vampire thrall drains the captain.
quote: the captain reacted like a cat and struck the shaman's head off with one blow from his jawbone axe.

summary: Sorin dominates a surviving warrior to serve as his guide to Ugin.
quote: You shall serve me,

summary: The Temur guide tells Sorin that dragons have been hunted to extinction and that the Spirit Dragon gave the Temur magic to fight corrupted dragons.
quote: But some say that the dragons became greedy and corrupt, so the Spirit Dragon gave us magic to fight them.

summary: The guide leads Sorin to a chasm where only huge bones lie, and Sorin refuses to believe it is Ugin.
quote: That cannot be Ugin.

summary: Sorin descends into the chasm, finds Ugin's skull in the ice and discovers Ugin is dead.
quote: Ugin was dead. And with him fell the hopes of countless worlds.

summary: Sorin fears Zendikar and then Innistrad will be consumed and says they are all doomed.
quote: We're all doomed,

summary: Sarkhan Vol, mind unraveling, returns to Tarkir in disgrace and begins to hear a voice.
quote: I return in disgrace because no other plane will have me.

summary: Sarkhan recalls Bolas sending him to the Eye of Ugin to watch, and being left blinded and sleeping.
quote: Bolas sent me to the Eye. He told me to wait.

summary: Sarkhan realizes Bolas treated him as a mere pawn and dismissed him as a dragon's toy.
quote: I am dismissed, a dragon's toy, tossed aside and useless.

summary: Flashback: Sarkhan grows up among the Mardu Horde as a feared battle mage and wing leader, scorching clans of the hinterlands.
quote: Talent with battle magic, and natural ferocity, made me feared among the Horde.

summary: Flashback: sick of endless blood, Sarkhan leaves his clan for the Qal Sisma Mountains, where a figure takes his shape and he joins the whisperers' chant of dragons.
quote: They remembered the old ones.

summary: Flashback: Sarkhan returns and the hordechief Zurgo demands his obedience, sending him against the Sultai.
quote: The Helmsmasher grudgingly sent me forth with a wing of riders to challenge the Sultai

summary: Flashback: in a stalemated battle Sarkhan kills the Sultai sorcerer, finds a quiet point, hears an ancient voice and a fire dragon bursts from his soul, burning everything.
quote: From my soul, a being of pure fire burst into the sky.

summary: Flashback: Sarkhan is cast to an alien desert world and spends years watching and following dragons, seeking a king to honor.
quote: I spent the next years watching and following, learning all I could about the dragons.

summary: Flashback: on Jund Sarkhan finds the dragons magnificent but unworthy and fights alongside tribes hunting Malactoth.
quote: Old Malactoth— he had been a true challenge.

summary: Sarkhan recalls the name Ugin as the dragon he should have heeded, and hears a voice telling him to find the doorway.
quote: The world remembers what its people have forgotten.

summary: Sarkhan resolves to seek the whisperers of the mountaintops again to find the door and make Tarkir strong again.
quote: I will make us strong again.

summary: Taigam's golden ship arrives at Kishla, pulled by undead sibsig, to collect the town's debt for Sidisi.
quote: A human Sultai enforcer lowered the gangplank for the leaders to enter the ship and head belowdecks.

summary: Flashback: Taigam, taught by Narset, leaves the Jeskai and travels to Purugir seeking work, drawing Sultai interest.
quote: He didn't set out to join another clan.

summary: Flashback: the rakshasa Ebirri offers Taigam power in the Sultai, and Taigam pledges his life to the rakshasa.
quote: Taigam swore his life in service of the rakshasa.

summary: Flashback: Taigam rises to chief advisor of Sidisi, who sends him to enforce her decrees, watched by Ebirri.
quote: Taigam rose to chief advisor of Sidisi, the kahn of the Sultai.

summary: Taigam humiliates an elder of Kishla, then has a guard take one of his three children.
quote: Now you have two,

summary: Jeskai monks kill the departing guard and burst into the ship to assassinate Taigam.
quote: Three human Jeskai monks stood with clenched fists.

summary: Ebirri fights the monks and kills two while Taigam, freeing himself, stabs the rakshasa, who then crushes a monk's head; Ebirri reminds Taigam he owns him.
quote: I own you,

summary: Taigam learns that Narset sent the surviving monk, has the monk crushed, and suspects the monks were zealots acting without her.
quote: They were zealots, most likely acting without her knowledge.

summary: Taigam resolves to handle the Jeskai threat himself and has the dead monks sized for golden uniforms.
quote: Taigam signaled the sibsig to keep the boat moving as he began to size the intact dead monks for golden uniforms.

summary: Kuhnde, a Jeskai monk, stands atop his mantis on a tower and watches the valley, vigilant against the mount he rides.
quote: Atop a red-roofed Jeskai tower, a monk named Kuhnde stood on his mantis and looked over the valley.

summary: In a flashback, the young Kuhnde is tested by the masters of the strongholds and found competent in all disciplines, though expert in none, so they recognize him as suited to be a mantis rider.
quote: He was competent in all the disciplines, although not an expert, but they all recognized in Kuhnde the skill set that was required of being a mantis rider.

summary: In a flashback, Kuhnde meets his mount on the same day; a rider shows him how dangerous a mantis is when a freed tether lets it cut the rider's hand.
quote: The rider removed one of the mantis's tethers and the insect lashed out, cutting the rider's hand.

summary: Kuhnde's mantis alerts him to a concealed amber orb of energy racing up the mountain, and he signals the mantis to intercept it.
quote: Kuhnde's mantis turned its head, alerting him to movement near the base of the mountain.

summary: Kuhnde leads the orb away from the monastery toward the valley lakes, then turns back and jabs it with his spear.
quote: He signaled the mantis to go lower, so they could lead the energy ball away from the monastery.

summary: Kuhnde's spear thrust makes the orb dissipate, and a phoenix emerges and attacks.
quote: There was a loud screech, one the monks in the monastery would have heard, and the orb dissipated. A phoenix emerged and attacked.

summary: Kuhnde has the mantis take the phoenix's attack and the mantis wounds the phoenix, which flees toward the monastery's library tower.
quote: It cut the phoenix with its longer claws, and blood and flame emerged from the wound.

summary: Kuhnde resolves to protect the library's scrolls with his life, as the Jeskai prize their words above gold.
quote: Kuhnde would lay down his life protecting them.

summary: Kuhnde impales the phoenix with his spear, but its flames burn the mantis's wings and both creatures fall and slide down the mountainside.
quote: His mantis began to fall and he knew why before he saw—its wings were burning.

summary: Kuhnde finds his mantis of twenty years dying and still trying to kill him.
quote: He approached it, his companion for twenty years, as it lay dying.

summary: Kuhnde kills his dying mantis with his spear to end its misery.
quote: With a quick, precise motion, Kuhnde impaled the mantis's head to end its misery

summary: Kuhnde decides against killing the injured phoenix, since it would only be reborn stronger; he rights it and strikes its beak with his spear shaft, beginning to tame it.
quote: He had never learned how to tame a phoenix, but he knew, given the time, he would master a new way.

summary: Kela and Dar walk toward Jigme Village to arbitrate a theft case while village children stare at their glowing dragon's eye marks.
quote: A handful of Jigme Village children were racing toward them along the far bank of the babbling river.

summary: A girl in a tree falls when her branch breaks but lands like a cat and shyly smiles at Kela.
quote: She landed soundlessly in a crouch like a cat on the side of the path.

summary: Dar scolds Kela for smiling and speaking, insisting the twins' justice rests on how they are perceived.
quote: You shall not show emotion. What we do, it's all about perception, Kela.

summary: Elder Ngabo welcomes the Arbiter Twins to Jigme in the square.
quote: I am Elder Ngabo. You honor us with your presence, Arbiter Twins.

summary: The court hears the case against Lotse Taring, accused of stealing nine baskets of apples; Kela and Dar listen in deep meditation.
quote: Nine baskets of apples had been stolen from the Village reserve.

summary: Waking in the Tower of Innocence, Kela does not know the verdict, feeling like a fraud, but decides to light her lamp, then changes her mind.
quote: But the only thing she felt in her soul was the weight of deception.

summary: Kela leaves her lamp unlit; Dar lights his, and the villagers declare Lotse guilty.
quote: Lotse was guilty. Dar had lit his lamp.

summary: At the celebration, Elder Ngabo drinks apple soup and dies, apparently poisoned.
quote: She raised her hands to her neck, clawing wildly, her face turning gray.

summary: The villagers blame Lotse for poisoning the elder and storm the prison to kill him.
quote: She was poisoned!" This voice was loud and sure. "It was the apples!

summary: Kela leaps between Lotse and a warrior's sword, demanding that he receive a trial.
quote: He should have a trial," she whispered.

summary: Kela invokes the Rules of the Reeds, and Dar reluctantly agrees to a quick judgment before the mob has Lotse's head.
quote: But we will be quick.

summary: Kela, locked in her tower, lights her lamp of innocence, producing two flames.
quote: Then she lit wick. The lamp of innocence ignited.

summary: The mob storms the towers, and Kela escapes out the window on the air currents, pursued by Dar.
quote: Kela sprang out through the window.

summary: Dar claims to know the judgment and knocks Kela from the air; she falls to the ground and refuses to concede.
quote: She lost her footing and her control and she plummeted to the ground.

summary: The twins fight the Combat of Clarity, and Kela, seeing everything clearly, defeats Dar.
quote: Kela leapt into a spinning strike and landed in a crouch on the ground with her knee on Dar's chest and her blade at his throat.

summary: Kela spares Dar and offers him balance, and the twins stand before the villagers as equals.
quote: For the first time, they stood together before the villagers as equals.

summary: Dar announces that Lotse will have a fair trial, and the girl from the tree rings the gong.
quote: The man will have a fair trial," Dar said.

summary: Narset meditates among a hundred monks in the plaza, outwardly serene while her mind races.
quote: But just because I look quiet and serene doesn't mean I am.

summary: Narset recalls growing up an outsider who retreated into imaginary worlds, then undertaking the Way of the Wandering Warrior and being appointed khan by the elders.
quote: my counsel was sought out by many regarding these matters, until the elders saw to appoint me the khan of the Jeskai.

summary: Narset secretly sticks her tongue out at a bored child during meditation.
quote: I stuck my tongue out quickly and he covered his mouth with both hands, apparently trying to stifle a gasp.

summary: Narset ends the session by reciting a traditional saying that she privately dislikes.
quote: Our own selves are the greatest obstacles to enlightenment,

summary: Narset slips away from her required solitary meditation, leaving a decoy with a melon for a head to fool her guard Shintan.
quote: I quickly constructed my decoy, dressed in the same clothes, complete with a melon for a head I had stored here the night before.

summary: Narset reads the Annals in the stronghold's depths, learning of clans working together against the dragons and of Ugin and Bolas, but cannot decipher Ugin's runes.
quote: I learned that a dragon named Ugin was connected to Tarkir in ways the khans couldn't comprehend, and that some had claimed Ugin was gone, but not dead.

summary: Returning to the pavilion, Narset finds eight Disowned orcs holding Shintan and her decoy destroyed.
quote: I made it to the rock face and climbed back up to the pavilion to find eight Abzan orcs standing within.

summary: Narset ambushes the orcs, killing one with a palm strike to the heart, kicking two, and turning their commander against his own soldiers.
quote: I landed in front of the orc and spun around, striking left of the center of the orc's chest, having timed his heart's pumping to stop it with my palm.

summary: Shintan frees himself and defeats his captors, and the two end the fight with orcs dead and wounded on the marble floor.
quote: The orcs lay, some dead, all bleeding, on the marble floor of the sacred temple.

summary: Shintan reports that an orc said Taigam hired them in revenge for an assassination attempt Narset allegedly sent; Narset denies knowing of any assassins.
quote: He said he and his kin were hired by the rat Taigam.

summary: The imprisoned orcs all tell the same story, but the elders accept that they are lying; Narset concludes Tarkir is sick with war.
quote: Tarkir was sick with war.

summary: Narset meditates atop a mountain peak, stops seeking an answer, and begins to dream of the worlds from her youth.
quote: The worlds from my youth rush toward me.

summary: Nahiri raises a stone rampart around a refugee camp, though she knows it will not hold against the monstrous creatures overrunning the plane.
quote: Nahiri, called the Lithomancer, surveyed her work and frowned.

summary: Sorin urges Nahiri to leave the refugees and focus on stopping the creatures before they spread to other worlds; Nahiri insists they are there to save the people.
quote: I'm here to stop these creatures, on this world, before they spread to others—to mine, or to yours.

summary: Sorin admits that they are not winning against the creatures.
quote: No," he said.

summary: Nahiri melts stone with an old spell and draws out a sword for Lian, telling her the world is hers to fight for.
quote: She pulled, and an elegant blade slid free of the molten rock.

summary: An enormous Eldrazi rises beyond the valley and the brood surges toward the camp.
quote: Then a figure, impossibly large, rose up behind the hills on the far side of the valley.

summary: Nahiri, Sorin and Lian fight the first wave of Eldrazi brood at the wall, but the titan's pull drains their magic.
quote: Nahiri could feel her mana spiraling away even as she gathered it.

summary: The plane begins to come apart as a crack in the world opens and the refugees are swept away.
quote: The plane was coming apart.

summary: Sorin flashes away and Lian is taken by the light; Nahiri grabs the sword and planeswalks off the dying world.
quote: Silently cursing herself, Nahiri grabbed the sword and left the world behind.

summary: Nahiri and Sorin regroup at a kor settlement in Akoum on Zendikar.
quote: Nahiri clutched the sword, the last trace of a now-dead world.

summary: Ugin appears as a luminous dragon, and Nahiri meets him for the first time.
quote: Then he was there with them: a massive, ethereal dragon, shining with blue-white light.

summary: Ugin reveals he watched the destruction without helping, in order to learn about the Eldrazi, and explains what they are and why they cannot simply be killed.
quote: They're called the Eldrazi," said Ugin, "and they devour entire worlds.

summary: Ugin proposes imprisoning the three true Eldrazi on a single plane, binding them with physical anchors and forcing them into dormancy.
quote: Bind them to one plane using their physical forms as anchors, and force them into dormancy.

summary: Ugin describes the ideal prison world, and Nahiri realizes he means Zendikar, refusing at first.
quote: What gives me the right to put everyone here in danger?

summary: Ugin explains he chose Zendikar because it has a protector, and asks for Nahiri's help rather than forcing her.
quote: No," said Ugin. "Because I also need your help.

summary: Nahiri decides that Zendikar will be the Eldrazi's prison and she their jailer, and agrees to the plan.
quote: Zendikar would be their prison, Nahiri their jailer, one world and one Planeswalker standing steadfast to protect all others.

summary: Over forty years, Nahiri pulls hedrons from the earth and Ugin etches them with runes, creating a trap and a lure for the Eldrazi.
quote: It took forty years of near-constant work.

summary: Nahiri warns Zendikar's peoples of the coming Eldrazi as the titans slowly approach the hedron-lit plane.
quote: Nahiri spread word throughout the plane of what was coming

summary: The three titans Ulamog, Kozilek, and Emrakul arrive on Zendikar, and Ugin and Sorin fight their brood as the titans march toward the hedron nexus.
quote: Ugin breathed his ghostfire, searing the Eldrazi brood with invisible flame.

summary: Nahiri, Sorin and Ugin focus their power in the Eye of Ugin and shift every hedron into its final position, completing the network.
quote: Every single hedron on the plane glowed as they shifted into new positions.

summary: The three Eldrazi stand petrified over Akoum and the chamber is sealed with a lock that requires three Planeswalkers to open.
quote: Looming above the highlands of Akoum, the three Eldrazi stood petrified, surrounded by a web of floating hedrons.

summary: Nahiri vows that her work is just beginning as she looks up at the imprisoned titans.
quote: My work is just beginning.

summary: Riza and his Abzan patrol of fifty march along the Salt Road, and Riza notes the smoke on the horizon is not a Mardu camp.
quote: But that is no Mardu encampment.

summary: The patrol finds a shepherds' summer camp destroyed, with every villager killed, and Riza orders the dead buried, fearing the horde of at least one hundred that did it.
quote: The small village lay in utter desolation. No survivors were left.

summary: The Mardu hordechief feasts on the loot and has his advisors plan the next raid while privately hiding his own self-doubt.
quote: The shepherds will be moving their flocks north to the villages for winter.

summary: A goblin spy tells the hordechief that an Abzan patrol half their size is tailing them and has seen the shepherd camp.
quote: An Abzan patrol is tailing us, only half a day's ride to the south.

summary: Riza decides against direct confrontation and orders the patrol to fall back to the Canyon Falls oasis to await a larger Salt Road patrol.
quote: We will fall back to the oasis at Canyon Falls and await the larger Salt Road patrol.

summary: The hordechief orders an immediate attack on the Abzan patrol and cuts off the tip of the quartermaster's finger when she questions him.
quote: who quickly snatched it, drew his knife, and sliced the tip off the pinky finger before she could react.

summary: The Mardu horde rides through the night; the Abzan spy buzzard reports it is turning to engage and will arrive before noon.
quote: The horde has turned south to engage us,

summary: Riza settles on retreating to the oasis canyon to nullify the Mardu cavalry advantage, ordering double time.
quote: Let's give ourselves the best odds.

summary: The hordechief hides his doubts about the gamble, believing he cannot show weakness if he wants to remain hordechief.
quote: To change course would be a sign of uncertainty.

summary: At the oasis, Riza orders a shield wall, hidden archers, and an ambush, and rallies his soldiers.
quote: Hide our archers among the boulders along the west rim of the canyon to keep the horde away from that side.

summary: The Mardu horde nears the oasis; the Abzan form a shield wall and endure a barrage of arrows.
quote: The air hummed with the flight of arrows.

summary: The Mardu horde splits in two to attack both ends of the canyon, and the hordechief glimpses an Abzan siege elephant tower.
quote: He rose in his saddle just in time to see the tower of the Abzan siege elephant poking through the haze in the distance…

summary: Sidisi sits crownless, obsessed with revenge on a goblin who took her crown, having fed her warning advisors to the Mother Crocodile.
quote: One by one, her most trusted advisors had warned her against the course of blind revenge

summary: In a flashback, Sidisi took the crown from the severed head of the previous khan and purged her rivals.
quote: The crown had once been taken by Sidisi herself, off of the freshly severed head of the previous khan.

summary: Jhinu is revealed to have framed three dead goblins for stealing her crown to win tax duties, and Sidisi has kept him alive as a living reminder of fates worse than death.
quote: She kept him alive as a reminder to all that there were fates worse than death.

summary: Sidisi mocks Jhinu that no relative is left to barter for his life and threatens to give him to the pits.
quote: If nobody is left who would barter for your life, maybe you are worthless.

summary: Sidisi explains she has raised an army by levying five percent of each province, then demanding the eldest born, with Rakshasa enforcing compliance.
quote: she had requested that all of the Sultai provinces provide five percent of their population to be enlisted into Sidisi's army.

summary: Jhinu presents recruits from the Niraj province, and Sidisi spots a thirteen-year-old youth among them.
quote: In the back was a youth, no more than thirteen years old.

summary: The youth attacks Sidisi with a poisoned dagger, but she hurls Jhinu into him and breaks the youth's neck.
quote: The youth attempted to regain his footing, but found the queen's tail around his neck.

summary: Sidisi identifies the poison on Jhinu as Silumgar's Breath, realizing the attack was a personal attempt on her life.
quote: It was known as Silumgar's Breath

summary: Sidisi kills Jhinu by thrusting the dagger into his chest rather than letting him suffer.
quote: Sidisi picked up the dagger and thrust it squarely into Jhinu's chest.

summary: Sidisi resolves never again to show mercy and plans to raise a vast army to destroy the Mardu and humiliate Zurgo.
quote: Soon, the great orc Zurgo himself would adorn her palace as her greatest prize.

summary: Zurgo surveys the Mardu army after defeating a Temur force and rallies it with a victory speech.
quote: Surrak has tested our borders," he shouted, "and we have shown him that they are strong.

summary: A goblin protests that Zurgo's broken rock was taken at the cost of his sister's life, and Zurgo stomps him to death to protect his authority.
quote: Zurgo raised his left foot as high as he could, then stomped on the goblin, dropping all his weight onto it.

summary: A messenger reveals the Temur attacked because a man calling himself Sarkhan turned into a dragon in Temur forests and the Temur mistook him for the new Mardu khan.
quote: He…they say he turned into a dragon. And breathed fire on them, took off, and flew farther into Temur territory.

summary: Zurgo declares Vol must die, and Varuk warns he is too dangerous, recalling Vol's desertion and dragonfire against the Mardu army.
quote: I was there when he turned into a great flying beast of flame and roasted your army with his breath.

summary: Zurgo plans to hide his real aim by marching the horde into the mountains to punish Surrak, despite his wing leaders' objections.
quote: Tomorrow, we move into the mountains," he said to them. "We will punish Surrak for his impudence.

summary: Unnatural snow falls as the Mardu enter the mountain valley, and Batar urges Zurgo to turn back.
quote: My khan, we must turn back. This is absurd. We are riding into a trap.

summary: Temur raiders strike the center of the Mardu line twice and vanish into the woods, killing over a hundred Mardu.
quote: Fifty Temur arranged in a column broke into our line, killed fifty-six, and disappeared back into the woods.

summary: Zurgo gives three young warriors new names for their first kills: Headtaker, Heartpiercer, and Neckwringer.
quote: Headtaker," Zurgo decreed.

summary: Batar challenges Zurgo for leadership of the clan.
quote: I challenge you for the right to lead this clan.

summary: Zurgo defeats Batar in single combat and kills him, stomping his head.
quote: Zurgo ran his sword straight through Batar's chest, threw the limp form to the ground, and stomped his great foot on the man's head.

summary: Varuk declares that Zurgo's horde fears him rather than serves him, and the horde follows Varuk home to Wingthrone, abandoning Zurgo.
quote: They once served you. Now they only fear you. And that means that you are not truly their khan.

summary: Left alone, Zurgo resolves to kill Vol, refusing to wipe Batar's blood from his blade until it mixes with Vol's.
quote: He would not clean it until it had mixed with Vol's.

summary: Zurgo kills a dying Temur woman after learning Vol went toward the Spirit Dragon's tomb, then rides there alone.
quote: He plunged his sword into the woman's throat and she stopped moving.

summary: Zurgo's riding-beast breaks a leg, and he leaves it to die and continues on alone.
quote: Zurgo left it to die and continued alone.

summary: Anafenza, newly khan for two weeks, climbs the First Tree barefoot and prepares to face the heads of the houses and one hated family member.
quote: Anafenza always climbed barefoot.

summary: The heads of the clan houses gather to swear kinship, and Anafenza receives them at the Amber Throne.
quote: The houses had elected Anafenza to be khan

summary: The last delegate, her cousin Oret, recognizes Anafenza and is seized with fear.
quote: Recognition. Then fear.

summary: At her command, an orc forces Oret to his knees, and Anafenza draws the Khan-Blade.
quote: Anafenza ascended the dais to her throne, and slowly drew her sword, the Khan-Blade, from its scabbard.

summary: In a flashback, thirteen-year-old Anafenza lives aboard her house's rolling fortress on the Salt Road.
quote: At thirteen, she had spent most of her life rumbling from city to city throughout the Abzan lands

summary: Anafenza is introduced to her cousin Oret and to Gvar Barzeel, a krumar orc raised by her uncle after the battle that killed his Mardu parents and her cousin.
quote: Gvar was a krumar, which meant he was not born in the Abzan.

summary: Oret insists the caravan continue to the capital rather than return to Kavah, citing dust storms.
quote: I must insist we continue to the capital.

summary: Anafenza lashes out at Gvar, insisting they are not family, and he replies that neither chose their family.
quote: We're not cousins, Gvar! We're not even family!

summary: Hakrez, the kin-tree warden, teaches Anafenza that the kin-tree belongs to blood-kin and bond-kin alike.
quote: This tree belongs to all of them.

summary: Undead mastodons rise from the sand and a Sultai war party ambushes the caravan fortress.
quote: A Sultai war party!" Anafenza saw dozens of archers take positions at the parapet.

summary: Ancestral spirits fight an undead mastodon, but the others crash into the fortress and Anafenza is thrown from the kin-tree as it splits.
quote: Anafenza couldn't focus, everything went sideways, and the Salt Road rushed up to toward her.

summary: Anafenza finds the kin-tree shattered and the warden Hakrez dead.
quote: Anafenza recognized the lifeless body of Hakrez, the kin-tree warden, whose breastplate was caved in.

summary: As the Sultai retreat, Anafenza discovers Abzan soldiers slaughtering their own kin at the fallen fortress.
quote: She saw Abzan butchering Abzan.

summary: Gvar tells Anafenza her parents are dead and is hit by an arrow as they flee into the wastes.
quote: Your parents are dead. As is my bond-father.

summary: Anafenza and Gvar share grapes during their march, and Gvar says the clan will demand justice for the betrayal.
quote: Our house was betrayed, but our clan will demand justice.

summary: Alone at a dead village tree, Anafenza weeps for her family.
quote: All she could see was her kin-tree, splintered and dead.

summary: Anafenza ambushes two traitorous Abzan pursuers, killing one with her sword.
quote: One of the men turned in time to receive the point of Anafenza's blade below his breastplate.

summary: Interrogated, the captured attacker names Oret as the member of her house who hired the Sultai.
quote: Oret. It was Oret.

summary: Back in the present, Anafenza coolly confronts Oret, who says he thought she was dead.
quote: You were dead.

summary: Anafenza scars Oret's face with the Khan-Blade, disowns him before the First Tree, declares him her enemy, and has Gvar, her brother, show him out.
quote: I disown you, Oret. You are no longer of my blood.

summary: Ajani travels across Theros, reflecting on gods and on Naya, and camps in the mountains hoping leonin will find him.
quote: He made camp in the fading light, without stealth or subterfuge.

summary: Ajani notices the night sky lacks its usual constellations and has a void where no star shines.
quote: Worse, in one corner of the sky, there was simply blankness, a void where no star shone.

summary: Ajani recalls that Elspeth left Dominaria for Mirrodin, which other planeswalkers now say is dead with Phyrexia returned.
quote: Then other Planeswalkers had spread the word: Mirrodin is dead. Phyrexia has returned.

summary: Seza's patrol finds Ajani at dawn and recognizes him.
quote: You are Seza," said Ajani, yawning, "and the last time I was here, you were too young to go out on patrol."

summary: Seza reveals that Brimaz is now king after Queen Omala died fighting humans, and that he declined vengeance.
quote: The queen, Omala, had died in battle with humans.

summary: Seza tells Ajani the gods vanished, leaving a ring of blank sky called the Moat of Oblivion.
quote: One day, the gods just... went away.

summary: Ajani reaches Tethmos and is reunited with Brimaz, who jokes about his title.
quote: Brimaz snorted, and soon the two leonin were chortling and embracing.

summary: Ajani asks Brimaz for help finding his friend Elspeth, and Brimaz points him to Lanathos.
quote: You should talk to Lanathos," said Brimaz.

summary: Lanathos tells the leonin the tale of Polukranos and the Champion of the Sun, who slays the hydra at the Plateau of the Four Winds.
quote: Polukranos, eater of poleis, beloved of the gods, was no more.

summary: Ajani introduces himself to Lanathos and asks about Elspeth; Lanathos eagerly asks where Ajani is from.
quote: There are people across the mountains? Leonin and human?

summary: Lanathos explains that the Champion of the Sun is a title, and that the latest champion killed Polukranos about a month ago.
quote: Very recently. During the Silence of the gods. A month ago, perhaps slightly more.

summary: Ajani realizes the latest Champion may be Elspeth, and Lanathos says she was seen at Akros, besieged by minotaurs.
quote: After she slew Polukranos, the Champion was spotted at Akros, which has been besieged by a horde of minotaurs.

summary: Ajani resolves to find Elspeth and help her.
quote: After all, the Champion always has companions.

summary: Sarkhan emerges in darkness on a snowy Temur tundra after passing through the flaming gate, with the gate gone and Ugin's voice silent.
quote: But now he was standing still in the darkness in the middle of a vast, snowy Temur tundra.

summary: Sarkhan grieves that Narset died and cries out to Ugin, realizing the voice in his head is gone.
quote: The ceaseless whispering, the constant flow of Ugin's words in his head—the voice was gone!

summary: Sarkhan falls to his knees, begging Ugin to speak, then laughs hysterically at the irony of wanting the whispers back.
quote: You can't be silent now!

summary: A storm of luminous clouds breaks over the tundra and dragons emerge from the tempest, to Sarkhan's amazement.
quote: A dragon!

summary: Sarkhan sees antlered dragons on Tarkir and realizes that the gate has taken him to Tarkir's past, as Narset's scrolls foretold.
quote: And it had led him to the past. It had led him here.

summary: Sarkhan follows the fledglings' flight across the tundra, believing this to be his path of healing for his plane.
quote: This was his path, the path that Ugin had set him on, the path of healing for his plane.

summary: A great dominant dragon arrives and leads the fledglings in formation to hunt.
quote: She had come to lead them. Now they would hunt.

summary: The dragons raid a human encampment in a basin while Sarkhan watches in awe.
quote: The brood descended like a barrage of flaming arrows.

summary: A fledgling's gaze welcomes Sarkhan to its brood and he begins to transform into a dragon.
quote: His transformation began without a conscious thought, without his permission

summary: A human warrior woman with a glowing red claw and her sabertooth kill two fledglings, interrupting Sarkhan's transformation.
quote: As the fallen dragon turned on her, she cut through its face from eye to jaw.

summary: The dominant dragon's fire drives off the warrior and the brood flies away into the night.
quote: And with a rush of wings and screeching cries, the brood disappeared into the night.

summary: Sarkhan, enraged, is about to attack the warrior but is stopped by a calm memory of how dragons brought balance, and his anger turns to awe at her.
quote: She was a survivor—no, a conqueror!—following a battle with dragons.

summary: Sarkhan resolves to make sure dragons are waiting for Narset when she lives again on Tarkir, believing the past is gone and this is a new Tarkir.
quote: when Narset lived again on Tarkir, there would be dragons waiting for her.

summary: Sarkhan embraces the new beginning, calling it his Tarkir.
quote: This was a new beginning, a new Tarkir—his Tarkir.

summary: The guide describes Tarkir's past, where dragons hatch from storms and the five clans fight for survival as dragon slayers.
quote: Here, in the past, the five clans of Tarkir still exist.

summary: Over millennia, Ugin's magic coalesced into dragon tempests that birthed five broods, each led by a dominant dragon revered by a clan.
quote: Over the millennia, the spirit dragon Ugin's magic coalesced into powerful storms on his native plane of Tarkir.

summary: Nicol Bolas and Ugin, long-time rivals, finally clash in the sky above Tarkir, and Sarkhan arrives to watch.
quote: Nicol Bolas and Ugin—two of the most powerful Planeswalkers the Multiverse has ever known—finally clashed in the sky above Tarkir.

summary: Sarkhan realizes the whispers in his head were Ugin's plea leading him across time, and that his choice will reforge Tarkir's fate.
quote: they were a plea from Ugin that had led Sarkhan across time to this place and this moment.

summary: Sarkhan, arrived in Tarkir's past, follows the woman with the dragon-claw staff up a mountain by her trail of marks.
quote: gouged two sweeping curves into it with the clawed staff she carried.

summary: Yasova's sabertooth tackles Sarkhan from behind and pins him in the snow.
quote: Something slammed into him from behind, huge and living and warm.

summary: Yasova questions Sarkhan, who says he follows the whispers of Ugin and thinks she may be his spirit guide.
quote: I seek the great dragon Ugin.

summary: Sarkhan gives his name; she greets him mockingly as 'khan of khans,' and he declines to claim dominion, bowing and flattering her as he once did Bolas.
quote: Yasova Dragonclaw of the Temur pays her respects to you, O khan of khans, and bids you welcome to her lands.

summary: Yasova threatens to kill Sarkhan unless he gives a reason to be spared; he kneels and offers to serve her.
quote: Give me a reason to spare you, Vol, or I'll kill you and be on my way.

summary: Sarkhan tells Yasova that in his homeland there are no dragons or dragon tempests, only bones, and that Ugin is long dead.
quote: Not in all of Tarkir," he said. "Only bones.

summary: Yasova confirms that she believes the dragons fall if Ugin dies, and Sarkhan realizes a storm guided him to her.
quote: If Ugin dies, the storms cease. The dragons fall.

summary: Yasova furiously rejects Sarkhan's claim that her people are better than the weak khans of his time, saying she has seen a paradise with no dragons.
quote: But I've seen the unwritten myself, seen a world with no dragons. And it was paradise.

summary: Yasova reveals that a great golden dragon appeared in her vision and asked her to chart the storms so that he could find and kill Ugin.
quote: He told me that if I showed him the way to the spirit dragon's lair…he would kill Ugin.

summary: Sarkhan realizes the dragon in her vision was Bolas, already on Tarkir in the past.
quote: Bolas was already here!

summary: Sarkhan transforms into a dragon, breathes fire to push Yasova aside rather than fight, and flies off to protect Ugin.
quote: With a kick from his powerful legs, Sarkhan Vol launched himself into the sky.

summary: Alesha leads the Mardu horde in an ambush of six dragons from Kolaghan's brood in a canyon.
quote: Her arrow struck the first one in the mouth, sending a stray bolt of lightning harmlessly to the ground.

summary: Mardu warriors drop from a bluff onto the swerving dragon and two drive swords deep into its flesh.
quote: But two Mardu—two who would be celebrated this night—drove swords into its flesh

summary: A dragon's lightning breath terrifies Alesha, recalling the scars on her back from an earlier dragon, and she leaps from her horse.
quote: a memory of past terror, when another spawn of Kolaghan's brood had given her the scars she wore on her back.

summary: A towering nameless orc stuns a dragon but holds back instead of killing it, and Gedruk Wingbreaker delivers the killing blow.
quote: It was Gedruk Wingbreaker who ran forward and hacked at the creature's neck before it could regain its balance.

summary: Alesha confronts the orc about holding back; he insults her as a human boy who thinks he is a woman.
quote: A human boy who thinks he's a woman?

summary: In a flashback, sixteen-year-old Alesha kills her first dragon with a spear and names herself Alesha, her grandmother's name, before the old khan and the horde.
quote: she pulled a spear from a dead man's back and plunged it into the beast's mouth, up into its brain.

summary: In the flashback, the old khan and horde shout Alesha's name without hesitation.
quote: And the whole gathered horde shouted "Alesha!" in reply.

summary: Alesha kills another dragon with a swing of her sword while it lunges at the nameless orc, and tells him to show who he is.
quote: I know who I am," Alesha said to him, still smiling. "Now show me who you are."

summary: The orc fights unorthodoxly, battering the dragon and making openings for allies, and the six dragons die at great cost.
quote: Six of Kolaghan's brood would never prey on the Mardu again.

summary: After the battle, Alesha hears the warriors' deeds and shouts out each new war name.
quote: she shouted the name for the horde to hear—with never a moment's hesitation.

summary: Three warriors testify that the nameless orc saved their lives, and Alesha rebukes him for thinking his deeds are not glorious enough, telling him to learn his place before choosing a name.
quote: When you learn what your place among the Mardu is, then you can choose a name.

summary: The orc declares he knows Alesha and names her 'Alesha, Who Smiles at Death,' and the Mardu shout her name.
quote: and I call you Alesha, Who Smiles at Death.

summary: Tasigur bores through a herald's account of Yala's dragon-slaying and perfunctorily thanks her.
quote: Your heroic deeds are a credit to the Sultai. Please accept my gratitude.

summary: At breakfast, an Abzan servant tasting Tasigur's food dies of poison.
quote: Poison!" Tasigur shouted, springing to his feet.

summary: Tasigur has Shidiqi take him to the rakshasa Khudal, who names Yala as the poisoner in exchange for the right to feed on the traitor's soul.
quote: Yala, whom you honored before your throne yesterday, has done this.

summary: Tasigur presents Yala with her husband's zombie bearing a necklace that is actually a garrote, whips her, and reads her mind.
quote: Please accept this token of my gratitude for your heroic deeds," Tasigur drawled.

summary: Finding no evidence of her treachery in her mind, Tasigur kills Yala in frustration.
quote: Snarling his frustration and disgust, he wrenched his fingers and snuffed out what little remained of her life.

summary: Khudal reveals the poison was his own, that he lied so he could feast on Yala's soul, and Tasigur, in rage, has robbed him of that prize.
quote: No," Khudal said. "The poison was mine."

summary: Khudal and Shidiqi abandon Tasigur with the prophecy 'And so the Sultai fall'; the naga and rakshasa leave the Sultai.
quote: And so the Sultai fall," the naga echoed, and she was gone, too.

summary: Without the naga's necromancy, the zombies disperse or crumble, and soldiers desert as Abzan and Jeskai raids grow.
quote: The months since had been one long slide into a perfect fulfillment of those prophetic words.

summary: A herald warns of a dragon, and Tasigur hides in his private chambers while it attacks outside.
quote: And there the khan cowered in fear until the noise died down.

summary: Tasigur stands barefoot on the Marang riverbank and offers the dragon Silumgar his jade throne, kneeling in terror as the dragon descends.
quote: Six of his soldiers came forward, carrying the throne he had forsaken.

summary: Daghatar convenes twenty Abzan advisors at Mer-Ek, and Reyhan and Merel argue between striking at Dromoka and enduring.
quote: We bring down Dromoka, and her brood will scatter.

summary: Merel warns that the first battle against Dromoka cost over a thousand soldiers with no damage to her, and Daghatar acknowledges the Abzan may be facing the end.
quote: we may be facing the end of the Abzan.

summary: Daghatar consults the Remembrance, which urges him to do what must be done and recalls his first crisis, when a patrol was captured by the Sultai.
quote: To suffer a defeat and yet lose none of your strength.

summary: Daghatar travels to the site of the first battle with Dromoka to meet her emissaries.
quote: On behalf of the Eternal, we welcome you. I am Sohemus.

summary: Dromoka lands and grants Daghatar an audience, laughing at his plea for peace.
quote: That will not be possible. Your tribe of necromancers is a stain on her land that she cannot tolerate.

summary: Dromoka explains that binding the dead to serve the living is necromancy, which she cannot tolerate, though she respects the Abzan.
quote: as long as your people are tainted by necromancy, our brood will continue to wipe yours clean from the desert.

summary: The Remembrance urges Daghatar to strike Dromoka, but he chooses instead to sacrifice it.
quote: Raise me up. Strike your enemy down, now.

summary: Daghatar shatters the Remembrance with the mace, destroying the ancestors it held.
quote: He slammed it down again, and again, until it shattered into a thousand shimmering shards.

summary: Daghatar orders every kin-tree uprooted and necromancy forbidden, and Dromoka nods; Merel warns of civil war.
quote: Uproot every kin-tree. The practice of necromancy is hereby forbidden.

summary: Shu Yun dictates a history of Tarkir at Dirgur and prepares to receive the arriving khans at his unprecedented summit.
quote: This meeting, this council of khans, was Shu Yun's desperate effort to improve the odds of survival.

summary: Alesha, Reyhan, Yasova, and Tasigur arrive at Dirgur and bicker.
quote: Such bravado!" said Tasigur.

summary: Shu Yun halts a quarrel and urges the khans to stand together against the dragons.
quote: We must stand together, or our ways of life will vanish from the world.

summary: Yasova confesses that she helped a malevolent dragon spirit attack Ugin in hopes of ending the storms.
quote: I saw that the storms would cease if I helped a malevolent dragon spirit kill the great Ugin.

summary: Yasova explains that the sar-khan encased Ugin in a stone cocoon after she healed him, causing the tempests to return fourfold.
quote: He encased Ugin in a great stone cocoon inscribed with draconic runes.

summary: Reyhan blames Yasova for the deaths of thousands, but Shu Yun interposes under his truce, and the khans forgive her.
quote: Shu Yun interposed himself between Reyhan and Yasova.

summary: The khans disagree over whether to open the cocoon, kill Ugin, or kill the brood-lords; Shu Yun insists on balance and seeking Ugin.
quote: The destruction of the dragons is no better than the destruction of the clans.

summary: Bells announce Silumgar's brood and Ojutai's brood, which merge and fly together toward Dirgur.
quote: Out over the water, the two massive flights of dragons raced toward each other, crashed together…and merged

summary: The khans realize someone leaked the summit, and Alesha suspects Shu Yun, who denies it; Tasigur has vanished.
quote: Someone must have told them about our little summit," said Reyhan.

summary: Tasigur's guards attack, and Alesha's party kills them.
quote: Alesha and her bodyguards charged, and the room erupted in chaos.

summary: Shu Yun takes the Annals scrolls from Quan to hide them and leaps from the window onto Silumgar's dragon, killing it with his tattooed palm.
quote: His dragon tattoo flashed with magical energy, and he slammed his palm into a very particular spot on the dragon's skull.

summary: Shu Yun hides the scroll case in a room beneath the stronghold and swallows the key.
quote: He shut the door, took the key, swallowed it with a shudder, and ran back to the courtyard.

summary: Shu Yun kneels before Ojutai and offers his life to spare the Jeskai; Ojutai freezes him to death.
quote: The khan of the Jeskai fell.

summary: Reyhan is killed by Silumgar while holding off dragons as Yasova and Alesha escape across the lake.
quote: Reyhan was felled by Silumgar himself.

summary: Ojutai declares through his aven translator that the Jeskai are no more, orders every ghostfire warrior killed, and commands Quan to erase the names of the clans.
quote: As of this day, there are no more clans. There are no more khans.

summary: Silumgar sleeps on Tasigur's throne while Shidiqi and zombies collar Tasigur and make him the dragon's trophy.
quote: After all, Tasigur," she said, "you are his finest trophy.

summary: Daghatar receives Yasova's letter about Reyhan's death and orders word sent to the dragonlord to crush the holdouts.
quote: Tell the dragonlord that if we move now, we can either force the remaining holdouts to surrender…or crush them for good.

summary: Alesha, Jagun, and Doshiyn encounter Kolaghan, who lets them pass without attack.
quote: The dragon's mouth closed. Alesha lowered her bow.

summary: Alesha throws down the Mardu khan's banner and decides that she and the Mardu will follow Kolaghan rather than kneel.
quote: We don't have to kneel," said Alesha, grinning. "Just try to keep up."

summary: Yasova leads her warriors to Ayagor and feeds a mammoth to Atarka as a gift, asking to stop fighting.
quote: I don't want to fight you anymore. I'm tired of fighting. That was a gift. Spare us, and there will be more.

summary: Yasova carves an ivory image of the Temur offering meat to Atarka and says the future is not yet written.
quote: The future isn't yet written," she said. "It's up to us to write it, together.

summary: Sarkhan is pulled back through time and finds himself before the weathered hedron cocoon, evidence that many years have passed.
quote: He was standing before the hedron cocoon, exactly where he had been a mere moment before

summary: Sarkhan sees a herd of dragons overhead and understands that the dragons survived, then transforms and joins them.
quote: And in his dragon form, Sarkhan Vol took to the sky.

summary: The herd roars with Sarkhan, and he sees changed land with five broods and new dragons from a tempest.
quote: As he shot back up into the herd, he was greeted by nothing less than the sight of a dragon tempest rupturing before him.

summary: A bell rings from a Mardu camp and an ancient dragon leads a herd of dragons up to meet Sarkhan; he sees the other timeline's rotting skull in her face.
quote: Shooting toward him was both the dragon of this now, flesh and blood and scales, and the dragon of the now that had been lost forever

summary: Sarkhan lands at the Mardu camp and is attacked by the goblin Vial Smasher, whom he knew as Ankle Shanker and who doesn't recognize him.
quote: You're here! You're alive! Just like the dragon.

summary: Sarkhan transforms to shield Vial Smasher from her own thrown vial of dragonfire.
quote: As it shattered on the ground, Sarkhan transformed into a dragon and dove in front of Vial Smasher

summary: Sarkhan meets Zurgo, now the bell-striker, who does not know Sarkhan and says no one says the word khan under Kolaghan Dragonlord.
quote: Kolaghan Dragonlord kill khan-sayers.

summary: Zurgo mocks the name Vol and raises his dull blade; Sarkhan flees into the sky, realizing no one knows him in this changed Tarkir.
quote: Both orc and goblin stood in paralyzed stillness as Sarkhan Vol launched himself into the sky.

summary: Sarkhan realizes Narset might be alive in this timeline and heads to Jeskai territory to find her.
quote: She would be here. She would be alive!

summary: Sarkhan learns that the dragon Ojutai rules the Jeskai and follows word of Narset to the Dragon's Eye Sanctuary.
quote: He followed word of her name up and up, ever closer to Ojutai's roost.

summary: Master Taigam tells Sarkhan that Narset was a heretic punished to the full extent of the law and is no more.
quote: Narset is no more.

summary: Taigam throws Sarkhan down the stairs; Sarkhan flies off in despair, resolving to wake Ugin to repair the timeline.
quote: It was time to wake the Spirit Dragon.

summary: Eight-year-old Narset, restless in a crowded marketplace, accidentally topples a stack of apples and is told to wait outside.
quote: She lifted her arm, holding the apple on display—as hundreds more rained down around her

summary: Free outside, Narset runs along the river and hears Ojutai's lesson across the distance, and asks to be his student; he nods.
quote: I want to be your student," she said. "Please, let me be your student."

summary: For three years Narset trains under Ojutai from afar by the riverbank.
quote: Over the next three years, Narset studied, trained, and practiced under the Great Teacher from afar.

summary: Dragonspeaker Ishai invites Narset to study at Dragon's Eye Sanctuary.
quote: To study under the Great Teacher.

summary: At fifteen, Narset defeats Taigam in a practice match and is named Master by Ojutai, the youngest he has ever named.
quote: At fifteen, she was the youngest master Ojutai had ever named.

summary: Atop the summit, Narset feels trapped by the sense that there is nothing more to learn and is unable to thank Ojutai.
quote: And just like that she was trapped.

summary: After a year of worsening restlessness, Narset descends the mountain and finds an ancient forbidden archive beneath Dragon's Eye.
quote: It had to be an ancient archive, a place that she had only heard of in legend, a place that Ojutai had all but forbidden.

summary: The scrolls contradict Ojutai's teaching by speaking of khans and dragons before him.
quote: And from what the scrolls said, it seemed that there had been dragons before Ojutai.

summary: Taigam catches Narset and threatens to report her for blasphemy, but she blasts past him.
quote: Then let him!" Narset erupted with power, blasting past Taigam and ignoring his screams.

summary: Narset searches archives under Cori Mountain and Riverwheel and learns of Ugin and the dragon tempests.
quote: She learned of a Spirit Dragon, Ugin, who was the source of all magic on the plane, as well as the dragon tempests.

summary: In the looted archive beneath Dirgur, Narset reads the last scroll about the khans' summit and discovers Ojutai led the attack on them, which also reveals Sarkhan.
quote: One of those dragons had been Ojutai.

summary: Narset's spark ignites and she is pulled toward another world, but at the last moment she pulls herself back.
quote: And then she was pulled backward with such a force as she had never felt before and ripped away from Tarkir.

summary: Years later, by the river bend, Ojutai asks Narset what she has learned, and she tells him she has learned the truth.
quote: I have learned the truth," she whispered.

summary: Narset thanks Ojutai and lets go, walking away from Tarkir.
quote: Her words were carried away on the winds of Tarkir as she let go.

summary: Zurgo, once the Mardu khan of another timeline, serves as Kolaghan's bell-striker, rousing warriors with his greatsword when she stirs to battle.
quote: Zurgo has been reduced to serving as an attendant to the dragonlord Kolaghan.

summary: Atarka's arrival and storms melt the Qal Sisma glaciers, and she wipes out the mammoths and most of the former Temur shamans.
quote: Atarka quickly devoured most of the shamans of the former Temur clan

summary: The surviving Atarka shamans secretly warn each other through the Wide Whisper as Atarka's purge begins.
quote: As the dragon's purge began, the shamans warned each other secretly

summary: Dromoka's law outlaws ancestor magic as necromancy, and a few renegade spirit speakers hide kin-trees.
quote: Ancestor magic, once practiced by the distant forebears of the modern-day Dromoka humanoids, is outlawed by the dragonlord as a form of necromancy.

summary: Anafenza is executed for kin-tree worship, but a ghostly figure like her is seen fighting alongside the Dromoka.
quote: However, she practiced ancient kin-tree worship, and for that she was executed.

summary: Sorin arrives on Tarkir, uneasy beneath the sun, searching for Ugin who may be dead and guided only by an oracle's vague visions.
quote: His only guide now was a cluster of vague impressions given to him by an oracle.

summary: A party of Atarka warriors mistakes Sorin for a Silumgar death-spawn and threatens to take his head.
quote: Your head will decorate a spear tonight.

summary: Sorin enthralls a warrior as a guide and learns from him that the khans fell, the dragons now rule, and Ugin dwells in the Haven.
quote: Ugin is the beating heart of the world. He dwells within the Haven.

summary: Sorin sees the hedron cocoon in a chasm and wonders if Nahiri was there.
quote: Lithomancy on Tarkir? Had Nahiri traveled here before him and bested the dragon?

summary: Sorin drains the thrall of what blood remains and uses blood magic to destroy the hedron shard and unmake the cocoon, freeing Ugin.
quote: The hedron shard crumbled to dust, and the cocoon began to crack.

summary: Ugin explodes from the ruins, recognizes Sorin, and says he was saved after Bolas attacked him using his own dragons.
quote: He thought me his rival for power, and attacked me. Used my own dragons against me.

summary: Sorin tells Ugin that over a thousand years have passed and the Eldrazi have escaped their hedron prison on Zendikar, partly through Nissa's choice.
quote: They're free." Sorin had the urge to press the matter, to needle Ugin, to make someone else shoulder the blame.

summary: Ugin asks about Nahiri, and Sorin evasively says she lives but is not on Zendikar; Ugin insists all three of them must work together.
quote: Let me be clear. It must be the three of us.

summary: Ugin agrees to join Sorin at the Eye of Ugin, and Sorin planeswalks away from Tarkir.
quote: I will join you at the Eye soon.

summary: At a military camp, soldiers argue about the Guardian, a spirit said to fight for Dromoka troops; Oret says he can tell them who she is.
quote: I'm the one who killed that spirit in life.

summary: In the flashback, Oret and Captain Anafenza flee a Kolaghan horde through a canyon after their fortress falls and their lines break.
quote: But here they were, their fortress lost and their lines broken, fleeing for their lives before the bulk of a Kolaghan horde.

summary: A Kolaghan orc kills Oret's ibex with a lightning spear and attacks him; Anafenza kills the orc by drawing out his life with golden-white light.
quote: It passed through him, pulling something unseen but vital from him as it passed, leaving him lifeless in the dust.

summary: Anafenza leads Oret to a kin-tree in a dead-end chamber, revealing that amber vessels and the carved tree anchor ancestor spirits.
quote: Spirits can be carried in amber, but I believe the tree is their anchor.

summary: Gvar Barzeel and dozens of Kolaghan warriors enter the chamber, and Anafenza calls on the tree's ancestors.
quote: Spirits of this tree, ancestors of my people, your descendants need you.

summary: Anafenza merges with the ancestor spirits and kills Gvar and his entire warband.
quote: Gvar, the shamans, all of the Kolaghan raiders—they didn't stand a chance.

summary: A dragon of Kolaghan's brood dives at Anafenza and is torn apart by a bolt of golden light made of spirits, while the rest flee.
quote: They moved as a massive bolt of golden light, and at its advance the dragon tried to reverse course.

summary: Oret's scalelord lands in the chamber, crushing the kin-tree and learning of Anafenza's necromancy.
quote: their scalelord descended into the chamber where, beneath its great weight, the ancient tree fell to splinters.

summary: Oret asks his scalelord to let him execute Anafenza himself, and the dragon agrees.
quote: Please, my scalelord, allow me to be the one to execute her.

summary: Oret beheads Anafenza as she kneels, whispering that it is not the end.
quote: This is not the end," he whispered to his captain.

summary: Oret is honored in Kavah, then secretly gathers the amber shards and plants a new tree with Anafenza's name carved in it, erasing it from maps so her spirit has an anchor.
quote: It was to be Anafenza's tree.

summary: Oret reveals he now travels the Dromoka lands to tell the truth of the Guardian.
quote: I now travel our territory to share the truth. She is, as Yeffa said, a guardian.

summary: Sidisi recalls her death by the knife and her revival as an undead naga, which took away her ability to feel pleasure.
quote: as the knife plunged into her heart, and the necromancers chanted the spell that would bring her back

summary: A caravan from Marang arrives with tribute, and a human sent by Jhinu offers Sidisi a purse of jewels for an audience.
quote: Jhinu sent me," he said, handing Sidisi a small purse of gems.

summary: Sidisi confronts the envoy about the short tribute and warns that he must speak to her, not to the dragon.
quote: Do you not believe that your Lord deserves his cut?

summary: The envoy reveals three vials of Jrung Orchid poison and asks to approach the dragon to kill him.
quote: Allow me to approach the dragon, and I can end his reign.

summary: The envoy throws a vial at Silumgar, who is unharmed, and Silumgar's poison breath engulfs the room.
quote: It sailed across the room and struck Silumgar's massive body.

summary: Sidisi drags the dying envoy to the sibsig pit and throws him in to be devoured.
quote: Sidisi unceremoniously tossed the man's near-lifeless body into the pit.

summary: Sidisi reveals she keeps a collection of poisons in the hole where her heart was, waiting for the day to take back power and make the naga rulers.
quote: On that day, she would take the power the dragon had stolen from her, and the naga would become what they were always meant to be—rulers of these lands.

summary: The hunting horn sounds across the mountains and a family of hidden ainok rise to answer it.
quote: The horn sounds, and they walk.

summary: Surrak leads a hunt for an enormous mountain krushok to feed Atarka, taking elk, saberclaws, yeti, and a hermit along the way.
quote: An offering like that could keep the dragonlord satisfied for almost a week.

summary: A sick-looking dragon of Atarka's brood circles the sledge before leaving, and Surrak notes the rule of the hunt: bring Atarka the meat or become the meal.
quote: We bring her the meat, or we become the meal.

summary: The hunters trap the krushok, but it breaks free and kills several before Surrak's second spears it.
quote: With a powerful thrust, he drove the spear upwards under the beast's great jaw.

summary: The mad dragon dives from the clouds, scorches the party, and begins eating the krushok meant for Atarka.
quote: It stomped over to the krushok, and took a gluttonous bite while the surviving hunters scattered into the treeline.

summary: Surrak confronts the dragon, drawing on the land's energy, and kills it with a single punch that breaks its neck.
quote: The dragon fell to the earth, neck broken.

summary: Trapped by a storm, Surrak uses the dragon's organ for dragonfire and the hunters eat dragon for the first time.
quote: Surrak had never eaten dragon before. It was delicious.

summary: Surrak delivers the offering to Atarka at the Ayagor with the traditional words.
quote: Great Atarka, dragonlord and protector. This is a gift. Spare us, and there will be more.

summary: Surrak's second tells Atarka that Surrak killed one of her brood; Atarka says 'Take care of it,' and Surrak defeats the second when he attacks with a knife.
quote: With a burst of speed, Surrak slammed his fist into his second's ribs, cracking several, and sending the knife clattering along the stone.

summary: Sarkhan reflects, in flight, that everyone he knew lives changed, except himself and Narset, and resolves to ask Ugin.
quote: Everyone lived, it seemed, save two. Sarkhan. And Narset.

summary: Sarkhan sees blue-white light rise from Ugin's canyon and is harried by ghostly dragons that then retreat.
quote: Soon the spirit was joined by others.

summary: Sarkhan finds the hedron cocoon crumbled and Ugin alive, projecting images of Tarkir's dragons on the canyon wall.
quote: There, at the end of the canyon, a luminous shape towered, wings outstretched.

summary: Ugin deduces from the hedron shard that it came from the Eye after his defeat, and asks who Sarkhan is.
quote: I'm applying logic.

summary: Sarkhan explains his history: Ugin's spirit whispered to him, Bolas sent him to the Eye, and he later traveled back in time to save Ugin.
quote: When I stepped through I traveled back, before the dragons died, and tipped the scales of history.

summary: Sarkhan names Bolas as the one who sent him to the Eye to release the Eldrazi, and Ugin contains him briefly in a sphere of force before releasing him.
quote: He wanted it opened, the devourers released. He never told me why.

summary: Ugin explains that Sarkhan's original Tarkir never existed, and that Sarkhan never was born in this history.
quote: you, Sarkhan Vol, stepped fully formed out of a shadow, a place that never existed.

summary: Ugin recounts that Sorin Markov woke him and spoke of foolishness at the Eye.
quote: An ally of mine, a vampire and a Planeswalker, woke me up and spoke to me of 'foolishness at the Eye.'

summary: Sarkhan thanks Ugin and flies off to find Narset, certain she lives again.
quote: I say she lives again, and I will find her.

summary: Sarkhan finds this timeline's Narset walking through the snow; she doesn't know him but has read secret histories about the sar-khan.
quote: About a dragon-man, a sar-khan, who came from something called the Unwritten

summary: Narset reveals she traveled beyond Tarkir; Sarkhan explains planeswalkers and that three are in the valley.
quote: Planeswalker," said Sarkhan. "That's what we're called.

summary: Narset goes to speak to Ugin and plans to study Atarka's ivory histories, content to stay on Tarkir for now; Sarkhan agrees.
quote: But this world has secrets enough. For right now…I'm right where I want to be.

summary: Sarkhan arrives on Tarkir, recalls his past and the ghost of Ugin urges him to find the doorway; he sets out for the mountains.
quote: who urges him to "find the doorway."

summary: Sorin fights through Temur hunters, makes a vampire guide and finds Ugin dead in the canyon, concluding the Multiverse is doomed.
quote: Ugin is long since dead, and Sorin concludes that the Multiverse is doomed.

summary: Six thousand years earlier, Nahiri and Sorin fail to save an unknown plane from the Eldrazi, then agree with Ugin to imprison the titans on Zendikar.
quote: The trap is sprung, the titans are subdued, and Nahiri settles in for a long vigil to keep them imprisoned.

summary: Zurgo, mad with rage after his Mardu refuse to follow his personal quest, kills the challenger and leaves alone to hunt Sarkhan.
quote: Zurgo's command is challenged, and he kills the challenger

summary: Narset leads Sarkhan to the Nexus and stays to hold off Zurgo, who kills her; Sarkhan swears vengeance and steps through the gate.
quote: Zurgo overpowers Narset, killing her.

summary: Sarkhan emerges in Tarkir's past, sees Atarka and Yasova, and realizes he has traveled back in time.
quote: He realizes the truth: he has traveled into Tarkir's past

summary: Yasova tells Sarkhan she follows a vision given by Bolas, and Sarkhan transforms into a dragon and flies off.
quote: Sarkhan transforms into a dragon and flies away.

summary: Bolas strikes down Ugin, Sarkhan wraps Ugin in a hedron cocoon, and is whisked back to an altered present; the dragon tempests intensify.
quote: Bolas strikes Ugin down as Sarkhan tumbles into the snow.

summary: Tasigur seeks out the dragon Silumgar and offers his allegiance for the dragon's help.
quote: his allegiance for the dragon's assistance.

summary: Daghatar destroys the Remembrance and pledges his clan to Dromoka's service.
quote: Daghatar destroys the Remembrance

summary: Dragons assault Dirgur Stronghold, Tasigur betrays the khans, Shu Yun offers his life to Ojutai, and Reyhan dies helping Yasova and Alesha escape; the clans fall.
quote: Reyhan dies during the fighting to secure an escape for Yasova and Alesha

summary: Sarkhan awakens in the altered present, unable to revive Ugin, and finds Kolaghan, Vial Smasher, Zurgo and Taigam changed and not knowing him.
quote: He encounters the dragonlord Kolaghan

summary: Sorin, with no memory of an earlier visit, destroys the cocoon and awakens Ugin, who tells him the Eldrazi are free.
quote: Sorin destroys the cocoon and awakens Ugin.

summary: Ugin insists it must be the three of them, and Sorin agrees to find Nahiri and meet Ugin on Zendikar.
quote: Reluctantly, Sorin agrees to seek out Nahiri and meet Ugin on Zendikar to stop the Eldrazi.

summary: Sarkhan finds Ugin awake, learns he was never born in this timeline, and finds Narset, a Planeswalker exile; both are content to remain on Tarkir.
quote: both Planeswalkers agree that they are exactly where they wish to be.

summary: The Eldrazi stir and Nahiri wakes from her long slumber, a thousand years before the great reawakening.
quote: The Eldrazi stirred. Nahiri woke.

summary: Flashback: Nahiri recalls living among the kor for centuries, teaching lithomancy and training them to guard the prison, before withdrawing in apathy to the Eye of Ugin.
quote: She had trained the kor to keep watch over the Eldrazi prison

summary: Zendikar breaks open; Nahiri senses the Eldrazi prison has been opened.
quote: the prison of the Eldrazi. It was open.

summary: Nahiri frees herself from her cocoon, goes to the great hedron, and sends a summons to Sorin and the Spirit Dragon.
quote: she sent her call into the Æther

summary: After waiting, Nahiri realizes Sorin and the Spirit Dragon have not come and she is alone.
quote: They hadn't come. Sorin hadn't come. She was alone.

summary: Nahiri crushes Eldrazi with an avalanche, then enters a ruined kor city in Ondu and remembers her old life.
quote: sent an avalanche to crush the abominations

summary: Nahiri finds a carving of herself with a Kozilek-like figure named 'Nahiri the Prophet, Voice of Talib', and collapses the building, blaming herself for calling Kozilek a god.
quote: "Nahiri the Prophet, Voice of Talib."

summary: Nahiri visits the hedron network's sites, burying the Eldrazi broods she finds, and determines she must stop them alone.
quote: But she was alone, and she would do it alone.

summary: Near the Eye of Ugin, Nahiri finds a spiked stone building where the hedron network was disturbed and is furious.
quote: Even as she approached, she could tell that this was the point where the hedron network had been disturbed.

summary: Nahiri fights and kills vampires at the building with a glowing-hot sword.
quote: her glowing sword cut through cold flesh

summary: Nahiri discovers a bloodstained altar and a statue of Ulamog, and realizes the vampires' sacrifices disrupted the hedron network.
quote: their rites had successfully disrupted the hedron network enough for the Eldrazi broods to spill forth.

summary: Nahiri reshapes the statue into a new hedron, holding off more vampires and Eldrazi while she works alone.
quote: and brought the walls down on them, then returned to her work.

summary: Nahiri completes the hedron and repairs the Eldrazi prison, driving the titans back into torpor.
quote: to link up the broken lines of the hedron network and repair the Eldrazi prison.

summary: Nahiri, angry that Sorin abandoned her, decides to find him and wake him, and opens a pathway through the Blind Eternities to another plane.
quote: eager to find her oldest friend.

summary: Kiora leaps onto the back of Arixmethes and reveals to Ajani and Elspeth that she is not Callaphe, then leaves them to the Monsoon.
quote: "Not even close," Kiora replied, smiling back at him.

summary: Kiora dives beneath the waves as Thassa, as the Great Eye, bursts from the water.
quote: Kiora cast a spell to aid her swimming

summary: On the sea bed Kiora calls to the krakens and leviathans Thassa kept in the deep and summons sea-beasts from many worlds.
quote: she gathered to her the essence of every sea-beast she had ever called her own.

summary: Kiora rises with her armada and sees Thassa on the Monsoon; Thassa sends Elspeth and Ajani away on a great wave.
quote: Thassa stepped off the deck of the Monsoon

summary: Thassa shifts into her triton form and summons the krakens of Theros as Arixmethes sides with her.
quote: He was also, for the moment, on Thassa's side.

summary: The two armies clash as hundreds of tritons arrive to watch; Thassa taunts Kiora.
quote: "Bear witness to the fall of the pretender!"

summary: Kiora tries to wrest Arixmethes from Thassa by bonding with his mind, but fails.
quote: You are not mine

summary: Kiora's serpent turns on her and devours dozens of tritons, and half her krakens turn against her.
quote: devouring dozens in one bite.

summary: Kiora banishes her serpent and the traitor krakens and falls, cushioning her fall with roots and vines from the sea floor.
quote: she pulled roots and vines up out of ground that had never seen the sun

summary: Thassa parts the sea into an arena, accuses Kiora of leading her people astray, and pins her to a boulder with the thrown bident.
quote: It slammed into her and pinned her to one of the boulders

summary: Kiora takes the bident and planeswalks away with it, leaving Thassa crying out in anguish.
quote: melted away into the void, Thassa's weapon still clutched in her hands.

summary: Ral leads Jace through the Undercity to show him something about Project Lightning Bug.
quote: Ral Zarek led the way through the sunken street

summary: Flashback: Maree suggests tracking Jace's long disappearances and Ral is appointed Head Researcher of Project Lightning Bug.
quote: Thus Ral had been appointed Head Researcher of a project to record and explain Beleren's disappearances.

summary: Flashback: Ral designs a tracking enchantment on Jace's cloak and a storm over the Tenth that turns planeswalk pulses into lightning.
quote: The drizzle field would magnify the tracking enchantment's small pulses into detectable cracks of lightning overhead

summary: Ral explains to Jace why he hides Planeswalkers from Niv-Mizzet and resents Jace for becoming the Guildpact.
quote: An outsider, who had done no work at all.

summary: Flashback: At Izzet headquarters Maree reveals she has replicated the detectors and found two new Planeswalker signals, threatening Ral's secret.
quote: other Planeswalkers coming and going from Ravnica.

summary: Niv-Mizzet sides with Maree and orders more power added to the storm amplifier.
quote: Finally he looked at Maree. "Do it."

summary: Ral and Jace watch from a Boros garrison for a Planeswalker Ral has been tracking, who does not appear.
quote: It's a Planeswalker I've been tracking.

summary: Jace confides that he does not remember his home and thinks of himself as Ravnican too, and Ral calls him Jace for the first time.
quote: That's the first time you've called me anything but 'Beleren.'

summary: Ral amplifies the storm atop Nivix, and the storm records Jace as a discontinuity while also placing him in the Tenth the whole time.
quote: The storm registered a discontinuity

summary: Niv-Mizzet declares the method unreliable and terminates Project Lightning Bug.
quote: "Project terminated," snarled the dragon
